verdict.rationale: Oneleet ships a sizable documented Public API (an OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec with 157 paths, plus a 25-path Auditor API), scoped service keys for automation, and an MCP server that acts with the user's full role permissions. However, the spec itself says the routes behind the web application are not part of the public API and reject service keys and OAuth tokens, so the vendor never claims full UI parity. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity commitment, evidence that UI-only actions (e.g., policy publishing, Trust Center setup, MDM remote actions) are exposed via the API, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Oneleet serves a downloadable OpenAPI 3.0.3 document for its Public API (157 paths)
The same host also serves the routes behind the Oneleet web application. Those routes aren't part of the public API
Use **service keys** for AI agent automation, MCP servers, and scripts to interact with your Oneleet workspace.
Once connected, the assistant acts as you. It can only see and do what your own role in the workspace allows
